              ⓘ how

              Hindsight, not a rule that ran: each paper trade since the restart, sold at its highest (max profit) or its lowest (max loss) minute-candle close within 6 hours after the entry, on the pool it was bought on, after the paper fees. Wicks, dust candles and one-candle glitches do not count; a pool that died counts as a total loss. The dot is what the rule (stop at −30%, take-profit at +1,000%, 6 hours) really made with the same trades; 'back above the entry' and 'rose further' count the trades whose best came after that sale. The raw top is the highest close of all, unfiltered, shown where it differs: one candle, dust volume, a dead pool or a level over the cap could not be sold there. Estimates and 15-minute candles are bounds. Nobody knows the top or the bottom in advance. Fake money, nothing is bought for real.

              ⓘ how

              Each radar round's best 5 coins (pools under 10 minutes old) go in here for 3.00 € each, at the price the radar saw, at the round's time; a coin only once. Green: the radar rated it good in that round. Sold by the paper account's rules on the pool's minute candles: the first close at −30% or lower is a stop, the first level of +1,000% or more that the next close confirms is a take-profit (at that level), else the close at 6 hours; a pool that died is a total loss; paper fees on both sides. Hindsight: the same coins sold at their best close within 6 hours (filtered like the account's best within 6 h), and at the raw top close, unfiltered, which one candle, dust volume, a dead pool or a level over the cap can make unsellable. Priced by the job after each scan, so a result shows about an hour after its 6 hours.

              How a coin is sold

              Fake money, no budget. Every scan buys the top pick (the first recommendation) for 50 € and the first 5 coins of the new-launches tab for 3 € each; a coin that is already held is not bought again, and one that was sold may be bought again the next time it is named. Each position is sold, all of it, by whichever comes first: the first minute candle that closes at 11 times the entry price (take-profit +1000%, booked at exactly that level), the first one that closes at 70% of it or lower (stop-loss −30%, booked at that close: a crash through the level fills worse, never better), at the first scan after about 6 hours (at that scan's price), or when the price or the liquidity is gone (rug). A scan without new candles checks both levels on its own price. Failing a filter sells nothing. Paper fees: 1% per trade, at least 0.10; the tip record keeps 0.5%, at least 0.81.

              Zero model
